evidence_text: High zinc intake induces intestinal metallothionein; metallothionein binds copper in intestinal cells and prevents systemic copper absorption.
scheduling_implication: High-dose zinc lowers copper absorption, especially with long-term use. Take them at least 4 hours apart and avoid prolonged high-dose zinc without copper.

evidence_text: Supplemental zinc at high doses has been reported to decrease magnesium absorption and disrupt magnesium balance.
scheduling_implication: Zinc can reduce the absorption or effect of magnesium. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Early human balance studies reported that increasing calcium intake can depress intestinal magnesium absorption, although later evidence is mixed.
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of magnesium. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Supplemental calcium has been reported to slightly decrease manganese bioavailability.

evidence_text: High calcium intake, especially as calcium phosphate or in phytate-containing meals, has been reported to reduce zinc absorption in some studies.

mechanism_type: thiomolybdate complex formation / copper absorption inhibition
evidence_text: Excess molybdenum with sulfur can form thiomolybdates that complex copper and prevent copper absorption.

evidence_text: N-acetyl cysteine can modulate copper homeostasis and can act as a thiol ligand or chelator under some experimental conditions (in vitro/ animal). But a human study at 600 mg/day for 2 weeks showed no change in plasma Cu.
evidence_scope: in vitro/in vivo; not clean oral co-administration PK
scheduling_implication: NAC can reduce the absorption or effect of copper. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Alpha-lipoic acid and its reduced form can chelate transition metals, including copper, in experimental settings.
scheduling_implication: Alpha-lipoic acid can reduce the absorption or effect of copper. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Alpha-lipoic acid has been described as binding divalent metal ions, including zinc, under experimental conditions.
scheduling_implication: Alpha-lipoic acid can reduce the absorption or effect of zinc. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Alpha-lipoic acid has been described as binding divalent metal ions, including manganese, under experimental conditions.

evidence_text: Vitamin D promotes calcium absorption in the gut and helps maintain serum calcium concentrations.
scheduling_implication: Taking vitamin D3 together with calcium (within about 1 hour) can help calcium work better.

evidence_text: The active form of vitamin D has been reported to slightly increase intestinal magnesium absorption.
scheduling_implication: Taking vitamin D3 together with magnesium (within about 1 hour) can help magnesium work better.

evidence_text: Enzymes involved in vitamin D synthesis and metabolism are magnesium dependent; magnesium status can influence vitamin D status.
scheduling_implication: Taking magnesium together with vitamin D3 (within about 1 hour) can help vitamin D3 work better.

evidence_text: Folate bioavailability can depend on zinc-dependent intestinal enzymes; low zinc has been associated with reduced folate absorption.
scheduling_implication: Taking zinc together with methylfolate (5-MTHF) (within about 1 hour) can help methylfolate (5-MTHF) work better.

evidence_text: High folic acid intake has been reported to impair zinc utilization in individuals with marginal zinc status.
scheduling_implication: Folic acid can reduce the absorption or effect of zinc. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Vitamin B6 has been proposed to facilitate magnesium absorption and cellular uptake; evidence is suggestive rather than definitive.
scheduling_implication: Taking vitamin B6 together with magnesium (within about 1 hour) can help magnesium work better.

evidence_text: Vitamin B12-dependent methionine synthase uses 5-methyltetrahydrofolate; B12 deficiency can trap folate as 5-methyl-THF and alter folate processing.
scheduling_implication: Taking vitamin B12 together with methylfolate (5-MTHF) (within about 1 hour) can help methylfolate (5-MTHF) work better.

evidence_text: Riboflavin-derived FAD is required by MTHFR, which converts 5,10-methylene-THF to 5-methyl-THF.
scheduling_implication: Taking riboflavin (vitamin B2) together with folic acid (within about 1 hour) can help folic acid work better.

evidence_text: Riboflavin is required for vitamin B6 metabolism.
scheduling_implication: Taking riboflavin (vitamin B2) together with vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) (within about 1 hour) can help vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) work better.

evidence_scope: chemical stability study, not direct oral PK

scheduling_implication: Take vitamin D3 with a fat-containing meal or together with dietary oils (fish/krill oil, MCT, seed oils) to improve its absorption.

scheduling_implication: Taking quercetin together with resveratrol (within about 1 hour) can help resveratrol work better.

scheduling_implication: Taking geranylgeraniol together with CoQ10 (within about 1 hour) can help CoQ10 work better.

scheduling_implication: Taking probiotics together with quercetin (within about 1 hour) can help quercetin work better.

scheduling_implication: Taking ubiquinol together with vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol) (within about 1 hour) can help vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol) work better.

mechanism_type: alternative methyl donor reduces folate methyl-trap stress
evidence_text: Betaine donates methyl groups via BHMT and supports homocysteine remethylation independent of the folate/B12 pathway, reducing reliance on the folate methyl pool.
scheduling_implication: Taking TMG (betaine) together with methylfolate (5-MTHF) (within about 1 hour) can help methylfolate (5-MTHF) work better.

mechanism_type: methyl-pool consumption (nicotinamide methylation via NNMT increases methyl-donor demand)
evidence_text: NMN supplementation can increase NAD-related nicotinamide flux and methylated nicotinamide metabolites such as MeNAM/MeXPY. Nicotinamide is methylated by NNMT using SAM as the methyl donor, linking NAD precursor metabolism to methyl-donor balance. TMG/betaine supports methyl-donor availability through homocysteine remethylation via the BHMT pathway, so co-use is a plausible methyl-burden offset rationale rather than a directly proven NMN-TMG co-dosing interaction.
evidence_scope: NAD-precursor/NAM methylation evidence plus betaine methyl-donor biochemistry; no direct NMN-TMG co-dosing trial verified
scheduling_implication: Taking NMN together with TMG (betaine) (within about 1 hour) can help TMG (betaine) work better.

mechanism_type: methyl-pool consumption (nicotinamide methylation via NNMT increases methyl-donor demand)
evidence_text: NR loading also raises nicotinamide flux and methyl utilization via NNMT, similar to NMN; TMG co-supplementation is commonly used.
scheduling_implication: Taking nicotinamide riboside together with TMG (betaine) (within about 1 hour) can help TMG (betaine) work better.

mechanism_type: methyl-pool consumption (nicotinamide methylation via NNMT increases methyl-donor demand)
evidence_text: Niacinamide also contributes to NNMT-driven methyl drain when used at high doses; TMG can offset.
scheduling_implication: Taking niacinamide together with TMG (betaine) (within about 1 hour) can help TMG (betaine) work better.

mechanism_type: enzymatic conversion of glucoraphanin to sulforaphane
evidence_text: Active myrosinase is required to hydrolyze glucoraphanin into bioactive sulforaphane; broccoli seed extracts lacking myrosinase yield substantially less sulforaphane after ingestion.
scheduling_implication: Taking myrosinase together with broccoli / glucoraphanin (within about 1 hour) can help broccoli / glucoraphanin work better.

scheduling_implication: Berberine can reduce the absorption or effect of probiotics. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: intestinal absorption inhibition via insoluble complex
evidence_text: Calcium carbonate reduces levothyroxine absorption by forming insoluble complexes in the gut; the levothyroxine label directs administration at least 4 hours apart from calcium carbonate, and review evidence supports a 2-4 hour separation for calcium formulations.
evidence_scope: prescription levothyroxine label / human absorption evidence
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: intestinal absorption inhibition via insoluble complex
evidence_text: Ferrous sulfate likely forms a ferric-thyroxine complex and reduces levothyroxine absorption; the levothyroxine label directs administration at least 4 hours apart from ferrous sulfate, with review evidence also associating iron supplementation with increased TSH.
evidence_scope: prescription levothyroxine label / human absorption evidence
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: formulation-specific adsorption / polyvalent-cation interference with levothyroxine absorption
evidence_text: Magnesium-containing antacid or laxative preparations can reduce levothyroxine absorption in formulation-specific contexts. The levothyroxine label identifies aluminum- and magnesium-containing hydroxide antacids as agents that can alter gastric acidity and reduce absorption; the broad magnesium mechanism remains minor because ordinary magnesium supplement forms are less certain than antacid preparations.
evidence_scope: prescription levothyroxine label plus formulation-specific antacid/laxative evidence
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Allicin / aged garlic organosulfurs have broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity in vitro and can transiently shift gut microbiota composition.
scheduling_implication: Garlic can reduce the absorption or effect of probiotics. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Coadministration of caffeine with theacrine has been reported to increase theacrine exposure, while the reverse effect on caffeine exposure is not the primary supported direction.
scheduling_implication: Taking caffeine together with theacrine (within about 1 hour) can help theacrine work better.

evidence_text: Carbidopa/levodopa (Sinemet) label: pyridoxine 10-25 mg orally 'may reverse the effects of levodopa' by speeding peripheral decarboxylation. Carbidopa blocks this, so the interaction matters only for levodopa without a decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g., Mucuna).
scheduling_implication: Only relevant to L-DOPA taken without carbidopa (e.g., Mucuna). Vitamin B6 speeds up L-DOPA breakdown outside the brain all day, so spacing the doses does not help; avoid high-dose vitamin B6 with these products.

mechanism_type: tannin-iron complex / non-heme iron absorption reduction
evidence_text: Green tea catechins reduce non-heme iron absorption by forming insoluble complexes in the gut.
scheduling_implication: Green tea can reduce the absorption or effect of iron. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

mechanism_type: polyphenol-iron complexation / reduced intestinal iron transport
evidence_text: Grape polyphenols, especially grape seed extract proanthocyanidins, can inhibit intestinal iron absorption or transport. The likely mechanisms include polyphenol-iron complexation in the intestinal lumen and reduced transepithelial iron transport. Some evidence suggests GSE may increase apical iron uptake through reducing activity, but net basolateral transfer and overall transport can still be reduced, so the model-ready direction is negative.
evidence_scope: polyphenol-class evidence plus grape seed extract / GSE intestinal cell evidence; stronger for intestinal transport/bioavailability than for a direct clinical scheduling trial
scheduling_implication: Grape polyphenols can reduce the absorption or effect of iron. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: large neutral amino acid transport competition at BBB
evidence_text: L-DOPA, phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan share the LAT1 transporter at the BBB; high LNAA load reduces L-DOPA brain entry.
scheduling_implication: Phenylalanine can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

from_mechanism_name: Essential amino acid blend (EAA / Perfect Amino)
evidence_text: EAA blends contain LNAAs that compete with L-DOPA for transport across the BBB.
scheduling_implication: Essential amino acids can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Gut microbiota convert anthocyanins to bioactive phenolic metabolites; bioavailability is microbiota-dependent.
scheduling_implication: Taking probiotics together with anthocyanins (within about 1 hour) can help anthocyanins work better.

evidence_text: Gut microbiota convert ellagic acid to urolithin A; conversion efficiency is highly individual.
scheduling_implication: Taking ellagic acid together with urolithin A (within about 1 hour) can help urolithin A work better.

evidence_text: NMN is converted to NAD+ via NMNAT enzymes; raises systemic NAD+ pool.
scheduling_implication: Taking NMN together with NAD+ (within about 1 hour) can help NAD+ work better.

evidence_text: NR is converted to NMN then NAD+; raises systemic NAD+ pool.
scheduling_implication: Taking nicotinamide riboside together with NAD+ (within about 1 hour) can help NAD+ work better.

mechanism_type: direct NAD+ precursor via salvage pathway
evidence_text: Niacinamide is converted to NAD+ through the salvage pathway (via the NAMPT enzyme) and raises the body's NAD+ pool.
scheduling_implication: Taking niacinamide together with NAD+ (within about 1 hour) can help NAD+ work better.

evidence_text: Pyridoxine is a non-active vitamin B6 vitamer that must be converted through the vitamin B6 salvage pathway to active PLP. Pyridoxal kinase phosphorylates pyridoxine, pyridoxamine, and pyridoxal using ATP-dependent chemistry, while PNPO is FMN/riboflavin-dependent. Magnesium may support ATP-dependent kinase chemistry, but the overall pyridoxine-to-PLP conversion is not exclusively magnesium-dependent.
evidence_scope: biochemical vitamin B6 salvage-pathway evidence; Mg-specific role is indirect and mainly tied to ATP-dependent kinase chemistry
scheduling_implication: Taking magnesium together with vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) (within about 1 hour) can help vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) work better.

mechanism_type: complementary metabolic signaling / intracellular berberine accumulation / LDLR-related lipid regulation
evidence_text: Berberine and resveratrol showed enhanced lipid-lowering activity in combination. Resveratrol increased intracellular berberine levels in hepatic L02 cells, and the combination increased LDL receptor expression more than either compound alone. This suggests resveratrol may increase cellular berberine availability, but the evidence is limited to cell studies.
evidence_scope: preclinical mouse and cell-line evidence; includes cell-line evidence that resveratrol increased intracellular berberine amount
scheduling_implication: Taking resveratrol together with berberine (within about 1 hour) can help berberine work better.

evidence_text: Ascorbate is an essential cofactor for prolyl hydroxylase and lysyl hydroxylase, enzymes required for collagen biosynthesis and stabilization.
evidence_scope: biochemical collagen synthesis mechanism plus human deficiency physiology
scheduling_implication: Taking vitamin C together with collagen peptides (within about 1 hour) can help collagen peptides work better.

mechanism_type: ribose-phosphate / PRPP support for adenine nucleotide resynthesis
evidence_text: D-ribose can enter ribose-phosphate/PRPP-related nucleotide resynthesis pathways and has been studied for restoring depleted myocardial ATP pools after energetic stress.
evidence_scope: human/physiology and pathway evidence; strongest in ischemia or energetic-stress contexts
scheduling_implication: Taking D-ribose together with ATP (within about 1 hour) can help ATP work better.

evidence_text: Long-term metformin use is associated with reduced vitamin B12 levels or deficiency, likely through impaired intestinal B12 absorption and calcium-dependent ileal uptake mechanisms.
scheduling_implication: Long-term metformin use lowers vitamin B12 status. This is not a timing issue; people on metformin may benefit from B12 supplementation or periodic B12 checks.

mechanism_type: microbial conversion of ellagitannins to urolithins
evidence_text: Pomegranate ellagitannins and ellagic acid require gut microbial metabolism for conversion into urolithins, including urolithin A; conversion capacity is highly individual.
scheduling_implication: Taking pomegranate ellagitannins together with urolithin A (within about 1 hour) can help urolithin A work better.

evidence_text: Human pharmacokinetic work suggests methylliberine increases caffeine exposure without a reciprocal effect, which may amplify stimulant effects when the two are stacked.
scheduling_implication: Taking methylliberine together with caffeine (within about 1 hour) can help caffeine work better.

mechanism_type: renal lithium-clearance modulation by caffeine intake
evidence_text: Lithium interactions often occur through renal function/sodium-water handling; case literature suggests caffeine intake changes can alter renal lithium clearance and serum lithium levels.
evidence_scope: case reports + renal lithium interaction pharmacology
scheduling_implication: Caffeine can reduce the absorption or effect of lithium. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

from_mechanism_name: Bacillus coagulans / Weizmannia coagulans protein-digestion probiotic
mechanism_type: probiotic-associated protein digestion / amino-acid appearance support
evidence_text: Bacillus coagulans strains, especially BC30/GBI-30, 6086, have been studied for improving protein digestion and postprandial amino-acid appearance. This suggests B. coagulans may improve absorption of co-ingested protein such as collagen peptides, but the evidence is not collagen-specific and not necessarily the exact SNZ-1969 or IDCC1201 strain.
evidence_scope: human protein/amino-acid absorption evidence for Bacillus coagulans strains; collagen-specific extrapolation
scheduling_implication: Taking Bacillus coagulans together with collagen peptides (within about 1 hour) can help collagen peptides work better.

evidence_text: Malate dehydrogenase catalyzes the reversible conversion of L-malate to oxaloacetate with coupled NAD+/NADH redox chemistry. This supports a biochemical metabolic-pool relation between supplemental malate and oxaloacetate, but not a strong same-window absorption or clinical interaction.
evidence_scope: basic biochemistry / enzymatic mechanism; supplement co-administration relevance indirect
scheduling_implication: Taking malate together with oxaloacetate (within about 1 hour) can help oxaloacetate work better.

evidence_text: Racetam-class nootropics have been linked to cholinergic mechanisms in preclinical and mechanistic literature. Choline donors may provide substrate support for acetylcholine-related pathways, but direct same-window human evidence for racetam-choline synergy is limited and mixed.
evidence_scope: preclinical/cholinergic mechanism literature; biohacker-practice rationale; limited direct human co-dosing evidence
scheduling_implication: Taking racetams together with choline (within about 1 hour) can help choline work better.

evidence_text: Ezetimibe inhibits NPC1L1-mediated intestinal sterol absorption, and NPC1L1 has been shown to regulate intestinal vitamin K absorption. This suggests ezetimibe may reduce vitamin K2 absorption, which matters most in anticoagulant or vitamin-K-sensitive contexts.
evidence_scope: NPC1L1 vitamin-K absorption mechanism; in vivo pharmacological evidence; clinical relevance context-dependent
scheduling_implication: Ezetimibe can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K2 (MK-7). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Ezetimibe inhibits intestinal NPC1L1 transport, and NPC1L1 is implicated in intestinal vitamin K absorption. This rule maps the vitamin-K-class mechanism to MK-4/K2 with conservative confidence.
evidence_scope: class-level extrapolation from vitamin K / NPC1L1 evidence
scheduling_implication: Ezetimibe can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K2 (MK-4). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Ezetimibe treatment reduced carotenoid transport in intestinal cell models and affected lipid transporters including NPC1L1, SR-BI, and ABCA1. This suggests ezetimibe may reduce carotenoid absorption, but direct human co-dosing evidence is limited.
evidence_scope: intestinal cell model / transporter mechanism; human supplement relevance uncertain
scheduling_implication: Ezetimibe can reduce the absorption or effect of mixed carotenoids. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Piperine is commonly used as a bioavailability enhancer and can increase curcuminoid exposure through metabolism- and transporter-related mechanisms.
evidence_scope: human bioavailability / pharmacokinetic and formulation literature
scheduling_implication: Taking piperine together with curcumin (within about 1 hour) can help curcumin work better.

evidence_text: Piperine acts as a broad bioavailability enhancer by inhibiting metabolism and transporters. It may increase resveratrol exposure, although the evidence is less direct than for curcumin.
evidence_scope: bioavailability-enhancer literature; extrapolated to resveratrol with moderate confidence
scheduling_implication: Taking piperine together with resveratrol (within about 1 hour) can help resveratrol work better.

mechanism_type: botanical antimicrobial activity against probiotic organisms
evidence_text: Oregano oil contains antimicrobial phytochemicals such as carvacrol and thymol. Because probiotic products contain live or viability-dependent organisms, antimicrobial botanical products may reduce compatibility when co-dosed in the same window.
evidence_scope: in vitro antimicrobial evidence / class-level probiotic compatibility inference
scheduling_implication: Oregano oil can reduce the absorption or effect of probiotics. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: fiber-associated reduction in lithium gastrointestinal absorption
evidence_text: Psyllium is a soluble fiber that can interfere with gastrointestinal absorption of some orally administered agents. Lithium is specifically noted as requiring separation from psyllium to reduce absorption interference.
evidence_scope: drug-supplement interaction reference; psyllium-specific absorption-timing guidance
scheduling_implication: Psyllium can reduce the absorption or effect of lithium. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

mechanism_type: prebiotic soluble fiber / fermentable substrate support
evidence_text: Partially hydrolyzed guar gum is a soluble prebiotic fiber that can alter gut microbiota composition and function. This supports a weak positive compatibility relationship with probiotic or microbiota-targeted products.
scheduling_implication: Taking galactomannan fiber together with probiotics (within about 1 hour) can help probiotics work better.

evidence_text: Larch arabinogalactan is a prebiotic fiber source that may support gut-microbiota-targeted interventions. The rule is a weak positive compatibility relation rather than a strong pharmacokinetic effect.
scheduling_implication: Taking arabinogalactan fiber together with probiotics (within about 1 hour) can help probiotics work better.

evidence_text: Xylo-oligosaccharides are prebiotic-type oligosaccharides used by gut microbes; same-day or same-window pairing with probiotic organisms is a plausible weak synbiotic support relation.
evidence_scope: prebiotic/synbiotic class evidence; ingredient-specific review accepted by user
scheduling_implication: Taking XOS fiber together with probiotics (within about 1 hour) can help probiotics work better.

evidence_text: Inulin and chicory-derived inulin are prebiotic carbohydrates that can be paired with probiotic organisms as synbiotic support; outcome remains strain-, dose-, and tolerance-dependent.
evidence_scope: inulin/probiotic synbiotic evidence inherited from existing extra-effect synbiotic logic
scheduling_implication: Taking inulin together with probiotics (within about 1 hour) can help probiotics work better.

evidence_text: Calcium and strontium are chemically similar divalent cations; high calcium intake can reduce strontium uptake, supporting separation when strontium is intentionally supplemented.
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of strontium. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Vitamin D2 is a vitamin D form; vitamin D promotes intestinal calcium absorption and supports calcium/phosphate homeostasis.
evidence_scope: authoritative vitamin D nutrient fact sheet; D2/D3 class inheritance
scheduling_implication: Taking vitamin D2 together with calcium (within about 1 hour) can help calcium work better.

evidence_text: Magnesium supports enzymes involved in vitamin D metabolism. This D2 rule is inherited from the existing magnesium-to-vitamin-D3 processing rule and represents chronic processing support rather than a direct absorption interaction.
evidence_scope: class inheritance from existing MID-MG -> MID-D3 rule; vitamin D metabolism cofactor literature
scheduling_implication: Taking magnesium together with vitamin D2 (within about 1 hour) can help vitamin D2 work better.

mechanism_type: concentrated polyphenol-iron complexation / reduced non-heme iron absorption
evidence_text: Concentrated olive polyphenol or hydroxytyrosol-rich extracts are polyphenol-dense products; polyphenol/tannin-rich matrices can reduce non-heme iron absorption via complexation. This rule is limited to concentrated olive polyphenol / hydroxytyrosol-rich extract and should not be generalized to olive oil or ordinary olive-containing foods.
evidence_scope: polyphenol-class iron absorption evidence; constrained olive-extract extrapolation
scheduling_implication: Olive polyphenols can reduce the absorption or effect of iron. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: polyphenol-iron complexation / reduced non-heme iron absorption
evidence_text: Bergamot phytosome is a concentrated polyphenol product; polyphenols bind non-heme iron in the gut, so it may slightly reduce iron absorption (weak, class-level evidence).
evidence_scope: polyphenol-class extrapolation; bergamot-specific timing evidence sparse
scheduling_implication: Bergamot extract can reduce the absorption or effect of iron. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: botanical antimicrobial activity against probiotic organisms
evidence_text: Concentrated antimicrobial botanical extracts such as clove, thyme, black walnut hull, wormwood/Artemisia, and pau d'Arco contain antimicrobial-leaning phytochemicals. Because probiotic products depend on live or viability-linked organisms, same-window co-dosing may reduce compatibility. This family rule is limited to concentrated antimicrobial botanical extracts and should not be generalized to ordinary culinary herb exposure.
evidence_scope: botanical antimicrobial class extrapolation; family-level consolidation to avoid rule explosion
scheduling_implication: Antimicrobial herbal extracts can reduce the absorption or effect of probiotics. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: NSAID-mediated reduction in renal lithium clearance
evidence_text: NSAIDs decrease renal blood flow, resulting in decreased renal lithium clearance and increased serum lithium concentrations.
evidence_scope: prescription lithium label / renal clearance interaction
scheduling_implication: NSAIDs can reduce the absorption or effect of lithium. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: gastric pH alteration / antacid-associated levothyroxine absorption reduction
evidence_text: Aluminum-containing antacid preparations can impair levothyroxine efficacy. The levothyroxine label lists aluminum hydroxide antacids among agents that may reduce absorption by altering gastric acidity, and review evidence reports impaired efficacy with aluminum hydroxide preparations.
evidence_scope: prescription levothyroxine label / systematic-review antacid evidence
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: adsorption or poorly soluble complex formation reducing levothyroxine absorption
evidence_text: Chromium picolinate may reduce levothyroxine bioavailability, plausibly through adsorption or poorly soluble complex formation. Evidence is limited relative to calcium and iron, with the review identifying a small non-randomized crossover study and recommending delayed chromium administration.
evidence_scope: limited human crossover evidence summarized in systematic review
scheduling_implication: Chromium can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: fiber adsorption / modest levothyroxine absorption reduction
evidence_text: Psyllium may modestly reduce levothyroxine absorption through fiber adsorption. The review describes broader fiber-associated levothyroxine efficacy concerns, while a small psyllium study found only a limited decrease that was considered unlikely to be clinically significant.
evidence_scope: low-medium clinical relevance represented as medium so mechanism aggregation retains the rule
scheduling_implication: Psyllium can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: CYP/P-glycoprotein induction reducing warfarin anticoagulant effect
evidence_text: Warfarin labeling identifies St John's wort as a botanical that can decrease warfarin effect, consistent with induction of drug-metabolizing pathways and reduced anticoagulation.
evidence_scope: FDA warfarin labeling / herb-drug interaction evidence
scheduling_implication: St John's wort can lower the levels or effect of warfarin throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether warfarin needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: gastric re-acidification improving pH-dependent dissolution and absorption
evidence_text: Human crossover studies show that betaine HCl rapidly re-acidifies the stomach under proton-pump-inhibitor-induced hypochlorhydria and substantially restores dasatinib exposure that was reduced by rabeprazole.
evidence_scope: human pharmacokinetic crossover + gastric pH crossover study
scheduling_implication: Taking betaine HCl together with dasatinib (within about 1 hour) can help dasatinib work better.

mechanism_type: intestinal uptake-transporter inhibition / reduced oral exposure
evidence_text: In a randomized crossover study, green-tea extract rich in EGCG reduced nadolol systemic exposure; complementary transport experiments supported inhibition of intestinal OATP1A2-mediated uptake.
evidence_scope: human randomized crossover pharmacokinetics + transporter experiments
scheduling_implication: Green tea can reduce the absorption or effect of nadolol. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: polyphenol/tannin complexation reducing non-heme iron absorption
evidence_text: A controlled stable-isotope trial found that tea consumed with an iron-containing meal reduced non-heme iron absorption, whereas separating tea by one hour attenuated the inhibitory effect.
scheduling_implication: Black tea can reduce the absorption or effect of iron. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

evidence_text: Clinical pharmacokinetic studies of Schisandra-derived preparations report substantial increases in dose-adjusted tacrolimus trough, Cmax, and AUC, consistent with CYP3A/P-gp-mediated interaction.
scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: schisandra can raise tacrolimus levels and increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

evidence_text: Human crossover data show reduced ciprofloxacin bioavailability with calcium carbonate; simultaneous calcium reduced relative bioavailability to approximately 60% of control.
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of ciprofloxacin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Clinical pharmacokinetic literature shows that magnesium-containing antacids can markedly reduce ciprofloxacin absorption through chelation.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of ciprofloxacin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: multivalent-cation chelation / severe reduction in gastrointestinal absorption
evidence_text: Human crossover data show a marked ciprofloxacin absorption loss with aluminum hydroxide; relative bioavailability was approximately 15% of control under simultaneous administration.
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of ciprofloxacin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: In a human study, ferrous sulfate substantially reduced ciprofloxacin AUC compared with ciprofloxacin alone, consistent with poorly absorbed chelate formation.
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of ciprofloxacin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: A zinc-containing multivitamin reduced ciprofloxacin AUC in a human study. Because the formulation contained multiple minerals, the zinc-specific contribution is not fully isolated.
evidence_scope: human pharmacokinetic study with a multi-mineral formulation
scheduling_implication: Zinc can reduce the absorption or effect of ciprofloxacin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Tetracycline-class literature supports reduced oral absorption with calcium-containing products through chelation; the magnitude varies by drug and formulation.
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of doxycycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: A human pharmacokinetic study found a large reduction in doxycycline exposure when administered with an aluminum/magnesium antacid; AUC fell from about 38.6 to 6.0 mg·h/L.
evidence_scope: human crossover pharmacokinetic study; combined Al/Mg antacid
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of doxycycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: A human pharmacokinetic study found a large reduction in doxycycline exposure with an aluminum/magnesium antacid; the study establishes a strong antacid-cation interaction although the individual Al and Mg contributions were not isolated.
evidence_scope: human crossover pharmacokinetic study; combined Al/Mg antacid
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of doxycycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Human interaction literature documents reduced absorption of doxycycline and other tetracyclines with iron salts through chelate formation.
evidence_scope: human interaction study + tetracycline interaction review
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of doxycycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of tetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Human tetracycline interaction literature shows substantial absorption inhibition with magnesium-containing products through chelation.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of tetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Human studies and reviews show substantial tetracycline absorption loss with iron salts through poorly absorbed chelate formation.
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of tetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Oxytetracycline belongs to the tetracycline class, for which calcium chelation reduces oral absorption; the exact oxytetracycline-specific magnitude is less well characterized.
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of oxytetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Oxytetracycline belongs to the tetracycline class, for which magnesium chelation reduces oral absorption; the exact oxytetracycline-specific magnitude is less well characterized.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of oxytetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Human studies of iron-tetracycline interactions include oxytetracycline and support clinically important absorption loss through chelate formation.
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of oxytetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Repeated St John's wort administration induces intestinal/hepatic CYP3A activity and decreases oral midazolam exposure.
scheduling_implication: St John's wort can lower the levels or effect of midazolam throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether midazolam needs monitoring or a dose change.

evidence_text: Repeated St John's wort administration reduced digoxin exposure in humans, consistent with intestinal P-glycoprotein induction.
scheduling_implication: St John's wort can lower the levels or effect of digoxin throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether digoxin needs monitoring or a dose change.

evidence_text: In renal-transplant patients, St John's wort markedly reduced dose-corrected tacrolimus exposure, consistent with CYP3A/P-glycoprotein induction.
scheduling_implication: St John's wort can lower the levels or effect of tacrolimus throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether tacrolimus needs monitoring or a dose change.

scheduling_implication: St John's wort can lower the levels or effect of cyclosporine throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether cyclosporine needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: CYP3A induction reducing simvastatin active-metabolite exposure
evidence_text: In a human crossover study, St John's wort reduced exposure to active simvastatin hydroxy-acid while pravastatin was not significantly affected, supporting a drug-specific CYP3A-mediated interaction rather than a universal statin-class effect.
scheduling_implication: St John's wort can lower the levels or effect of simvastatin throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether simvastatin needs monitoring or a dose change.

scheduling_implication: Use with caution: piperine can raise phenytoin levels, which may increase its side effects.

mechanism_type: sustained gastric-pH elevation reducing pH-dependent dasatinib solubility and absorption
evidence_text: Dasatinib exposure is pH-dependent. The current label reports omeprazole reducing dasatinib AUC by 43% and Cmax by 42%, and recommends avoiding proton-pump inhibitors.
evidence_scope: current prescription labeling / human drug-interaction pharmacokinetics
scheduling_implication: Proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs) can lower the levels or effect of dasatinib throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether dasatinib needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: gastric-pH elevation reducing pH-dependent dasatinib solubility and absorption
evidence_text: The current dasatinib label reports that famotidine given 10 hours before dasatinib reduced mean AUC by 61% and Cmax by 63%; H2 antagonists should not be coadministered.
evidence_scope: current prescription labeling / human drug-interaction pharmacokinetics
scheduling_implication: H2 blockers (e.g., famotidine) can lower the levels or effect of dasatinib throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether dasatinib needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: antacid-mediated gastric-pH change reducing dasatinib absorption
evidence_text: Simultaneous aluminum/magnesium hydroxide with dasatinib reduced mean dasatinib AUC by 55% and Cmax by 58%; giving the antacid 2 hours earlier avoided the AUC reduction.
evidence_scope: current prescription labeling / human drug-interaction pharmacokinetics
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of dasatinib. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

mechanism_type: sustained gastric-pH elevation reducing pH-dependent erlotinib solubility and exposure
evidence_text: Erlotinib solubility decreases as gastric pH rises. Omeprazole reduced erlotinib AUC by 46% and Cmax by 61% in label pharmacokinetic data.
evidence_scope: current prescription labeling / human drug-interaction pharmacokinetics
scheduling_implication: Proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs) can lower the levels or effect of erlotinib throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether erlotinib needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: gastric-pH elevation reducing pH-dependent erlotinib absorption
evidence_text: Ranitidine given 2 hours before erlotinib reduced AUC by 33% and Cmax by 54%; staggered administration substantially attenuated the interaction.
evidence_scope: current prescription labeling / human drug-interaction pharmacokinetics
scheduling_implication: H2 blockers (e.g., famotidine) can reduce the absorption or effect of erlotinib. Take erlotinib at least 2 hours before or 10 hours after H2 blockers (e.g., famotidine).

scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: ketoconazole can raise erlotinib levels and increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

evidence_text: Human studies and pooled evidence show increased oral cyclosporine exposure and bioavailability with grapefruit juice.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: grapefruit can raise cyclosporine levels and increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: Grapefruit juice increased oral midazolam Cmax and AUC in a human crossover study, consistent with inhibition of presystemic CYP3A metabolism.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Use with caution: grapefruit can raise midazolam levels, which may increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: Grapefruit juice increased triazolam AUC and Cmax in a randomized crossover study.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Use with caution: grapefruit can raise triazolam levels, which may increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: Human studies and clinical reviews support increased nifedipine bioavailability/exposure with grapefruit, although the magnitude is more variable than for felodipine.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Use with caution: grapefruit can raise nifedipine levels, which may increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: In a human trial, grapefruit juice increased diazepam AUC approximately 3.2-fold and Cmax approximately 1.5-fold.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Use with caution: grapefruit can raise diazepam levels, which may increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: Human studies show several-fold increases in simvastatin and simvastatin-acid exposure with grapefruit juice through intestinal CYP3A4 inhibition.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: grapefruit can raise simvastatin levels and increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: Tadalafil labeling predicts that grapefruit juice, as a CYP3A inhibitor, can increase tadalafil exposure; direct tadalafil-grapefruit interaction studies are limited.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Use with caution: grapefruit can raise tadalafil levels, which may increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: Tacrolimus labeling identifies grapefruit/grapefruit juice as a CYP3A inhibitor that can increase tacrolimus whole-blood trough concentrations and recommends avoidance.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: grapefruit can raise tacrolimus levels and increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: intestinal CYP3A inhibition reducing presystemic metabolism and increasing oral exposure
evidence_text: Erlotinib labeling lists grapefruit/grapefruit juice among CYP3A4 inhibitors that can increase erlotinib exposure and recommends avoidance or dose adjustment if severe reactions occur.
evidence_scope: human grapefruit-drug pharmacokinetics and/or current prescription labeling
scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: grapefruit can raise erlotinib levels and increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

evidence_text: Isoniazid can cause pyridoxine deficiency; labeling attributes this in part to competition with pyridoxal phosphate and recommends pyridoxine in patients predisposed to neuropathy.
evidence_scope: current prescription labeling / established antitubercular pharmacology
scheduling_implication: Isoniazid can lower the levels or effect of vitamin B6 throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether vitamin B6 needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: CYP1A2 inhibition markedly reducing caffeine clearance
evidence_text: In a double-blind crossover study, fluvoxamine reduced apparent oral caffeine clearance from about 105 to 9.1 mL/min and prolonged caffeine half-life from about 4.9 to 56 hours.
scheduling_implication: Use with caution: fluvoxamine can raise caffeine levels, which may increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: modest CYP1A2-related increase in fluvoxamine metabolism / reduced exposure
evidence_text: A randomized crossover study reported that repeated caffeine intake modestly reduced fluvoxamine AUC, while effects on fluvoxamine pharmacodynamics were not significant.
evidence_scope: human crossover pharmacokinetic study; reverse-direction effect is substantially smaller than fluvoxamine's effect on caffeine
scheduling_implication: Caffeine can lower the levels or effect of fluvoxamine throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether fluvoxamine needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: delayed gastric emptying reducing absorption rate / peak concentration
evidence_text: After the first tirzepatide 5 mg dose, acetaminophen Cmax was reduced by about 55% and Tmax was delayed by about 1 hour; overall AUC was not meaningfully changed and the gastric-emptying effect diminished with repeated dosing.
evidence_scope: current tirzepatide prescription labeling / human drug-interaction pharmacokinetics
scheduling_implication: Tirzepatide can reduce the absorption or effect of acetaminophen. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: delayed gastric emptying reducing oral-contraceptive absorption/exposure
evidence_text: With a first tirzepatide 5 mg dose, an ethinyl-estradiol/norgestimate oral contraceptive showed approximately 59% lower ethinyl-estradiol Cmax and about 20% lower AUC.
evidence_scope: current tirzepatide prescription labeling / human drug-interaction pharmacokinetics
scheduling_implication: Tirzepatide can lower the levels or effect of oral contraceptives (ethinyl estradiol) throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether oral contraceptives (ethinyl estradiol) needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: multivalent-cation chelation reducing fluoroquinolone gastrointestinal absorption
evidence_text: Aluminum-containing antacids can markedly reduce oral fluoroquinolone bioavailability through chelation.
evidence_scope: human fluoroquinolone interaction review / clinically relevant chelation mechanism
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of fluoroquinolone antibiotics. Take them 2–4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: multivalent-cation chelation reducing fluoroquinolone gastrointestinal absorption
evidence_text: Magnesium-containing antacids/mineral products can markedly reduce oral fluoroquinolone bioavailability through chelation.
evidence_scope: human fluoroquinolone interaction review / clinically relevant chelation mechanism
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of fluoroquinolone antibiotics. Take them 2–4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: multivalent-cation chelation reducing fluoroquinolone gastrointestinal absorption
evidence_text: Iron salts can reduce oral fluoroquinolone absorption through poorly absorbed metal-drug complexes.
evidence_scope: human fluoroquinolone interaction review / clinically relevant chelation mechanism
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of fluoroquinolone antibiotics. Take them 2–4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: multivalent-cation chelation reducing fluoroquinolone gastrointestinal absorption
evidence_text: Calcium can reduce oral fluoroquinolone absorption; magnitude varies by fluoroquinolone and food/mineral formulation.
evidence_scope: human fluoroquinolone interaction review / clinically relevant chelation mechanism
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of fluoroquinolone antibiotics. Take them 2–4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: multivalent-cation chelation reducing fluoroquinolone gastrointestinal absorption
evidence_text: Zinc-containing mineral products can reduce fluoroquinolone absorption through cation chelation; magnitude is drug/formulation dependent.
evidence_scope: human fluoroquinolone interaction review / clinically relevant chelation mechanism
scheduling_implication: Zinc can reduce the absorption or effect of fluoroquinolone antibiotics. Take them 2–4 hours apart.

mechanism_type: CYP3A inhibition/induction altering tacrolimus systemic exposure
evidence_text: Tacrolimus labeling lists ketoconazole among strong CYP3A inhibitors that can increase tacrolimus whole-blood trough concentrations.
scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: ketoconazole can raise tacrolimus levels and increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

mechanism_type: CYP3A inhibition/induction altering tacrolimus systemic exposure
evidence_text: Tacrolimus labeling lists rifampin among strong CYP3A inducers that can decrease tacrolimus whole-blood trough concentrations.
scheduling_implication: Rifampin can lower the levels or effect of tacrolimus throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether tacrolimus needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: CYP3A inhibition/induction altering tacrolimus systemic exposure
evidence_text: Tacrolimus labeling lists phenobarbital among strong CYP3A inducers that can decrease tacrolimus whole-blood trough concentrations.
scheduling_implication: Phenobarbital can lower the levels or effect of tacrolimus throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether tacrolimus needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: CYP3A inhibition/induction altering tacrolimus systemic exposure
evidence_text: Tacrolimus labeling lists phenytoin among strong CYP3A inducers that can decrease tacrolimus whole-blood trough concentrations.
scheduling_implication: Phenytoin can lower the levels or effect of tacrolimus throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether tacrolimus needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: CYP3A inhibition/induction altering tacrolimus systemic exposure
evidence_text: Tacrolimus labeling lists carbamazepine among strong CYP3A inducers that can decrease tacrolimus whole-blood trough concentrations.
scheduling_implication: Carbamazepine can lower the levels or effect of tacrolimus throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether tacrolimus needs monitoring or a dose change.

mechanism_type: food/calcium matrix reduces levothyroxine absorption on coadministration
evidence_text: A crossover pharmacokinetic study in 10 volunteers found lower levothyroxine exposure with concurrent cow's milk than with levothyroxine alone. This supports avoiding simultaneous administration; it does not establish a milk-specific four-hour interval or the same effect size for every milk powder formulation.
evidence_scope: small human cow's-milk absorption study; extrapolated to reconstituted milk powders
scheduling_implication: Milk / dairy can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 1 hour apart.

mechanism_type: dairy calcium chelation reducing tetracycline absorption
evidence_text: Tetracycline HCl label states that food and some dairy products interfere with absorption (alongside Al/Ca/Mg antacids, iron, zinc). A 2023 review of tetracycline-class drugs cites Leyden (1985): tetracycline absorption fell ~65% when taken with milk (81% with iron, 46% with food). The label gives no hour-specific separation for dairy.
evidence_scope: FDA label + review of human PK studies
scheduling_implication: Milk / dairy can reduce the absorption or effect of tetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

mechanism_type: dairy calcium chelation (smaller effect for doxycycline)
evidence_text: Single-dose crossover in 9 fasted healthy volunteers (doxycycline 200 mg with 300 mL milk vs water): Cmax fell 24% and absorption fell 9-53% (mean ~30%) (Meyer 1989). Doryx MPC label: a high-fat meal lowered Cmax ~30% with no significant AUC change, and the label allows taking it with food or milk if GI upset occurs. Other small studies found no significant effect of milk.
evidence_scope: human PK crossover, n=9; FDA label
scheduling_implication: Milk / dairy can reduce the absorption or effect of doxycycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

mechanism_type: dairy calcium chelation reducing ciprofloxacin absorption
evidence_text: Randomized crossover in 7 healthy volunteers (ciprofloxacin 500 mg with 300 mL water, milk or yogurt): milk cut Cmax 36% and yogurt cut it 47%, and AUC fell 30-36%. CIPRO label section 2.4: avoid taking with dairy products or calcium-fortified juices alone, though it may be taken with a meal that contains them. For multivalent-cation products, take CIPRO 2 h before or 6 h after.
evidence_scope: human PK crossover, n=7; FDA label
scheduling_implication: Milk / dairy can reduce the absorption or effect of ciprofloxacin. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: OTC enteric-coated bisacodyl label: 'do not use within 1 hour after taking an antacid or milk.' UK Dulcolax SmPC: milk and antacids may weaken the enteric coating, which can cause dyspepsia and gastric irritation. No PK magnitude is reported; the effect is early release in the stomach rather than measured exposure loss.
scheduling_implication: Milk / dairy can reduce the absorption or effect of bisacodyl. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

from_mechanism_name: Antacid / gastric-pH-raising mineral salt (Ca carbonate, Mg/Al hydroxide, Na bicarbonate)
mechanism_type: gastric pH rise dissolving enteric coating early
evidence_text: OTC enteric-coated bisacodyl label: 'do not use within 1 hour after taking an antacid or milk.' UK SmPC: antacids may reduce the coating's resistance, causing gastric irritation and early release. No PK magnitude is reported.
scheduling_implication: Antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of bisacodyl. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

mechanism_type: sustained gastric pH rise dissolving enteric coating early
evidence_text: UK Dulcolax SmPC section 4.2 says the coated tablets should not be taken with products that reduce upper-GI acidity, 'such as milk, antacids or proton pump inhibitors, in order not to prematurely dissolve the enteric coating.' No PK study quantifies the effect.
scheduling_implication: Proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs) can lower the levels or effect of bisacodyl throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether bisacodyl needs monitoring or a dose change.

evidence_text: Sinemet label: iron salts (including iron-containing multivitamins) can chelate levodopa and carbidopa and reduce their bioavailability, so co-administer with caution. Human PK data (Campbell et al., ferrous sulfate 325 mg; reported levodopa AUC reduction ~30-50%) could not be fetched for confirmation this session.
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 2 hours apart.

mechanism_type: large neutral amino acid competition (gut + BBB LAT1)
evidence_text: Nutt 1984 (NEJM, n=9 PD patients with fluctuations): high-protein meals and oral phenylalanine, leucine or isoleucine (100 mg/kg) reversed the clinical effect of IV levodopa without lowering plasma levodopa, which points to competition at brain (BBB) transport; glycine and lysine had no effect. Meals also cut peak plasma levodopa 29%. Sinemet label: levodopa competes with certain amino acids for gut transport, and high-protein diets may delay or impair absorption.
evidence_scope: human clinical study, n=9; FDA label
scheduling_implication: Whey protein can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Nutt 1984 (NEJM, n=9): oral leucine or isoleucine at 100 mg/kg reversed the therapeutic effect of infused levodopa (LNAA competition at BBB transport); valine was not tested. Sinemet label notes amino-acid competition for levodopa transport.
evidence_scope: human clinical study, n=9; FDA label
scheduling_implication: BCAAs can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Nutt 1984 (NEJM, n=9): oral leucine 100 mg/kg reversed the clinical response to infused levodopa without changing plasma levodopa, consistent with LAT1 competition at the BBB.
scheduling_implication: Leucine can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Tyrosine is a large neutral amino acid that shares LAT1 transport with levodopa. Nutt 1984 showed LNAA competition (phenylalanine, leucine, isoleucine) reverses levodopa response, but did not test tyrosine. Sinemet label notes amino-acid competition in general.
evidence_scope: mechanistic inference from human LNAA study
scheduling_implication: Tyrosine can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Tryptophan is an LAT1 substrate and so competes with levodopa by mechanism. Nutt 1984 showed the LNAA effect with phenylalanine, leucine and isoleucine but did not test tryptophan.
evidence_scope: mechanistic inference from human LNAA study
scheduling_implication: Tryptophan can reduce the absorption or effect of L-DOPA (e.g., Mucuna). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Cefdinir label: a 60 mg elemental iron supplement cut the extent of cefdinir absorption 80%, and a multivitamin with 10 mg iron cut it 31%. Take cefdinir at least 2 h before or after the supplement.
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of cefdinir. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: Cefdinir label: an Al/Mg hydroxide antacid taken with cefdinir cut Cmax and AUC ~40% and delayed Tmax 1 h. Take cefdinir at least 2 h before or after the antacid.
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of cefdinir. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: Cefdinir label: an Al/Mg hydroxide antacid cut cefdinir Cmax and AUC ~40%; separate by at least 2 h. The study used a combined Al/Mg antacid, so the Mg(OH)2-alone effect is an inference.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium hydroxide antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of cefdinir. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: Zithromax label Table 14 (n=10): Al hydroxide 1350 mg plus Mg hydroxide 1200 mg lowered azithromycin Cmax ~24% (ratio 0.765) with AUC essentially unchanged (ratio 0.984). The current label gives no explicit separation instruction.
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of azithromycin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Zithromax label Table 14 (n=10): a combined Al/Mg hydroxide antacid lowered azithromycin Cmax ~24% with AUC unchanged.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium hydroxide antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of azithromycin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Cuprimine label: oral iron reduces the effect of penicillamine, and 2 h should elapse between the two. In 6 healthy men given penicillamine 500 mg, ferrous sulfate cut plasma levels ~65% (to 35% of fasting), an antacid cut them ~34%, and food ~48% (Osman 1983).
scheduling_implication: Iron can reduce the absorption or effect of penicillamine. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: Cuprimine label: give penicillamine at least 1 h apart from any drug, food, milk, antacid, zinc or iron preparation to limit metal binding in the gut, and avoid mineral supplements. No quantitative zinc PK data were found.
scheduling_implication: Zinc can reduce the absorption or effect of penicillamine. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

evidence_text: Cuprimine label: food, antacids and iron reduce penicillamine absorption, mineral supplements should not be given, and penicillamine should be at least 1 h apart from antacids. Osman 1983 (n=6): an antacid (type not stated in the abstract) cut penicillamine plasma levels ~34%.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of penicillamine. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

evidence_text: Cuprimine label: antacids reduce penicillamine absorption; give at least 1 h apart. Osman 1983 (6 healthy men): an antacid cut penicillamine plasma levels ~34%.
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of penicillamine. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

evidence_text: Cuprimine label lists milk among the agents to separate by at least 1 h and says mineral supplements may block the response. No study quantifies calcium specifically.
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of penicillamine. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

mechanism_type: Al/Mg hydroxide antacid reducing MPA absorption
evidence_text: Myfortic label: in 12 stable kidney transplant patients, 30 mL of Mg/Al hydroxide antacid lowered MPA Cmax 25% and AUC 37%; do not give simultaneously. CellCept label: Mg or Al hydroxide antacids lower MPA exposure and should be given at least 2 h after CellCept.
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of mycophenolate. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

mechanism_type: Al/Mg hydroxide antacid reducing MPA absorption
evidence_text: Myfortic label: Mg/Al hydroxide antacid lowered MPA Cmax 25% and AUC 37% (n=12). CellCept label: give magnesium- or aluminum-hydroxide antacids at least 2 h after CellCept.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium hydroxide antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of mycophenolate. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: Kirch et al. 1981 (Clin Pharmacol Ther 30:429): calcium co-administration lowered atenolol Cmax 51% and AUC(0-inf) ~32% (5818 to 3935 ng*h/mL), but extended half-life from 6.2 to 11.0 h, causing accumulation with multiple dosing. That partly offsets the loss at steady state.
scheduling_implication: Calcium can reduce the absorption or effect of atenolol. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: Brown et al. 1976 (NEJM; Latin-square study, 10 healthy volunteers, digoxin 0.75 mg): 6-day urinary digoxin excretion fell from 40.1% (control) to 30.7% with Al hydroxide (~23% relative), 27.1% with Mg hydroxide, and 23.4% with kaolin-pectin. The Lanoxin label lists antacids among agents that lower digoxin concentrations.
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of digoxin. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: Penttila 1975 (crossover, 7 volunteers): zinc sulfate (45 mg Zn) taken with tetracycline 500 mg cut serum levels, AUC and urinary excretion ~30%; there was no significant effect on doxycycline. The tetracycline label states that zinc-containing preparations impair absorption.
evidence_scope: human PK crossover, n=7; FDA label
scheduling_implication: Zinc can reduce the absorption or effect of tetracycline. Take them at least 3 hours apart.

evidence_text: Macrodantin label: antacids containing magnesium trisilicate, taken with nitrofurantoin, 'reduce both the rate and extent of absorption.' The evidence covers Mg trisilicate (an adsorbent silicate) only, not Mg oxide or citrate supplements.
scheduling_implication: Magnesium can reduce the absorption or effect of nitrofurantoin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: Health Canada isoniazid product monograph (pdp-Isoniazid): aluminum hydroxide gel decreases GI absorption of isoniazid, so isoniazid should be taken at least 1 h before the antacid. Current US DailyMed isoniazid tablet labels checked did not mention antacids.
scheduling_implication: Aluminum antacids can reduce the absorption or effect of isoniazid. Take them at least 1 hour apart.

from_mechanism_name: Adsorbent binder / activated charcoal or clay
evidence_text: Crossover in 6 healthy volunteers: 50 g activated charcoal given immediately after digoxin cut digoxin absorption ~98%; given 1 h later, the inhibition was considerably smaller. The Lanoxin label lists activated charcoal among agents that lower digoxin concentrations.
evidence_scope: human PK crossover, n=6; FDA label
scheduling_implication: Activated charcoal or clay binders can reduce the absorption or effect of digoxin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

from_mechanism_name: Adsorbent binder / activated charcoal or clay
evidence_text: The Synthroid label says bile acid sequestrants, ion-exchange resins and phosphate binders decrease levothyroxine absorption and calls for 4 h separation, but it does not name activated charcoal. Endotext notes charcoal can prevent GI absorption of drugs in thyroxine overdose but gives no quantitative data. No PK study of charcoal at supplement doses was found.
scheduling_implication: Activated charcoal or clay binders can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

from_mechanism_name: Adsorbent binder / activated charcoal or clay
evidence_text: No confirmed human study or label statement on activated charcoal or other adsorbents with ethinyl estradiol. The rule rests on charcoal's non-specific adsorption and on possible interruption of EE enterohepatic recirculation, which is theoretical.
scheduling_implication: Activated charcoal or clay binders can reduce the absorption or effect of oral contraceptives (ethinyl estradiol). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

from_mechanism_name: Antacid / gastric-pH-raising mineral salt (Ca carbonate, Mg/Al hydroxide, Na bicarbonate)
mechanism_type: GI alkalinization increasing amphetamine absorption (and urinary alkalinization reducing excretion)
evidence_text: Adderall labeling states that gastrointestinal alkalinizing agents (e.g., sodium bicarbonate) increase absorption of amphetamines and urinary alkalinizers decrease urinary excretion, increasing blood levels; the current label says co-administration with GI alkalinizing agents should be avoided. The magnitude is not quantified in the label.
scheduling_implication: Avoid this combination unless a clinician approves: antacids can raise amphetamine (Adderall) levels and increase its side effects.

evidence_text: Adderall labeling lists GI acidifying agents (ascorbic acid, fruit juices, glutamic acid HCl) as lowering amphetamine absorption and blood levels; the intervention is to increase the dose based on clinical response, not to avoid the combination. No human PK magnitude is given, and the effect of ordinary supplemental vitamin C doses is not quantified.
scheduling_implication: Vitamin C can reduce the absorption or effect of amphetamine (Adderall). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Vyvanse label states that urinary acidifying agents (e.g., ascorbic acid) decrease amphetamine blood levels and efficacy by increasing urinary excretion; the intervention is to increase the dose based on clinical response. The label gives no magnitude, and how much typical vitamin C doses acidify urine is uncertain.
scheduling_implication: Vitamin C can lower the levels or effect of lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) needs monitoring or a dose change.

evidence_text: The Vyvanse label states that urinary alkalinizing agents (e.g., sodium bicarbonate) increase amphetamine blood levels and potentiate its action, and that co-administration of VYVANSE with urinary alkalinizing agents should be avoided. The label gives no numeric magnitude.
scheduling_implication: Use with caution: sodium bicarbonate can raise lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) levels, which may increase its side effects. Spacing the doses does not help.

evidence_text: Cholestyramine labeling reports reduced serum or red-cell folate with long-term use and advises considering folic acid supplementation. It instructs taking other drugs at least 1 h before or 4-6 h after the resin. No quantified PK study of folic acid with the resin was found.
scheduling_implication: Cholestyramine can reduce the absorption or effect of folic acid. Take folic acid at least 1 hour before or 4-6 hours after cholestyramine.

evidence_text: Cholestyramine labeling reports reduced serum and red-cell folate with chronic use, which supports a folate effect in general. Direct data on food folate or reduced folates (e.g., methylfolate) with the resin are lacking, so this rule is extrapolated from the folic acid statement.
scheduling_implication: Cholestyramine can reduce the absorption or effect of methylfolate (5-MTHF). Take methylfolate (5-MTHF) at least 1 hour before or 4-6 hours after cholestyramine.

evidence_text: The Zetia label reports that concomitant cholestyramine decreased the mean AUC of total ezetimibe by about 55%. It instructs dosing ezetimibe at least 2 h before or at least 4 h after a bile acid sequestrant.
scheduling_implication: Cholestyramine can reduce the absorption or effect of ezetimibe. Take ezetimibe at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after cholestyramine.

evidence_text: The CellCept label reports that MPA AUC decreased about 40% in healthy volunteers given MMF 1.5 g after cholestyramine pretreatment (4 g three times daily for 4 days), because the resin interrupts MPA enterohepatic recirculation. The current label advises monitoring efficacy rather than stating 'avoid'.
scheduling_implication: Cholestyramine can lower the levels or effect of mycophenolate throughout the day, so spacing the doses does not help. If both are used regularly, ask a clinician whether mycophenolate needs monitoring or a dose change.

evidence_text: In a Welchol label interaction study, co-administration reduced levothyroxine AUC by 22% and Cmax by 33%. Giving levothyroxine 4 h before colesevelam abolished the effect (AUC +1%), and postmarketing reports describe elevated TSH. The label instructs giving thyroid hormone 4 h before Welchol.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of thyroid hormone (levothyroxine). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: In the Welchol label, co-administration reduced ethinyl estradiol AUC and Cmax by 24% each. With a 1 h gap the AUC fell 18%, and with a 4 h gap it fell 12%. The label instructs taking the oral contraceptive at least 4 h before Welchol.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of oral contraceptives (ethinyl estradiol). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Welchol label cites postmarketing reports of increased seizure activity or decreased phenytoin levels in patients taking phenytoin. It instructs giving phenytoin 4 h before Welchol. No controlled PK magnitude is reported.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of phenytoin. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: In the Welchol label, co-administration decreased cyclosporine AUC by 34% and Cmax by 44%. The label instructs giving cyclosporine (a narrow therapeutic index drug) at least 4 h before Welchol and monitoring drug levels.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of cyclosporine. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Welchol label warns that colesevelam may decrease absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K, and instructs patients on oral vitamin supplements to take them at least 4 h before Welchol. No quantified PK data for vitamin A are given.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin A (retinol). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Welchol label warns that colesevelam may decrease absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K, and instructs patients on oral vitamin supplements to take them at least 4 h before Welchol. No quantified PK data for vitamin D are given.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin D3. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Welchol label warns that colesevelam may decrease absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K, and instructs patients on oral vitamin supplements to take them at least 4 h before Welchol. No quantified PK data for vitamin E are given.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin E. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Welchol label warns that colesevelam may decrease absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K, and instructs patients on oral vitamin supplements to take them at least 4 h before Welchol. No quantified PK data for vitamin K are given.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K1. Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Welchol label warns of decreased absorption of vitamin K (as a class) and asks for vitamin supplements to be taken at least 4 h before. NIH ODS notes that bile acid sequestrants can reduce vitamin K absorption. No data specific to K2 (menaquinones) exist; the rule is extrapolated from the lipophilic vitamin K class.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K2 (MK-4). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Welchol label warns of decreased absorption of vitamin K (as a class) and asks for vitamin supplements to be taken at least 4 h before. NIH ODS notes that bile acid sequestrants can reduce vitamin K absorption. No data specific to K2 MK-7 exist; the rule is extrapolated from the lipophilic vitamin K class.
scheduling_implication: Colesevelam can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K2 (MK-7). Take them at least 4 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Xenical label states that orlistat reduces absorption of some fat-soluble vitamins: low vitamin D levels occurred in 12.0% on orlistat vs 6.6% on placebo over 2 years. It recommends a multivitamin taken at least 2 h before or after orlistat (e.g., at bedtime). In obese adolescents, vitamin D levels fell on orlistat despite a daily multivitamin.
scheduling_implication: Orlistat can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin D3. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Xenical label states that vitamin K absorption may be decreased with orlistat and that vitamin K levels tended to decline in treated subjects. Warfarin users need coagulation monitoring, and vitamins should be taken at least 2 h apart from orlistat. NIH ODS also notes reduced vitamin K absorption with orlistat.
scheduling_implication: Orlistat can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K1. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Xenical label and NIH ODS state that orlistat can reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamin K, through lipase inhibition and fat malabsorption. There are no menaquinone-specific (K2/MK-7) data; the rule is extrapolated from vitamin K as a class.
scheduling_implication: Orlistat can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K2 (MK-4). Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Xenical label and NIH ODS state that orlistat can reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamin K, through lipase inhibition and fat malabsorption. There are no menaquinone-specific (K2/MK-7) data; the rule is extrapolated from vitamin K as a class.
scheduling_implication: Orlistat can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin K2 (MK-7). Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: In a PK study cited in the Xenical label, orlistat reduced absorption of a beta-carotene supplement by about 30%; low vitamin A levels occurred in 2.2% vs 1.0% on placebo. The effect on supplemental preformed vitamin A is stated as unknown. A multivitamin is advised at least 2 h before or after orlistat.
scheduling_implication: Orlistat can reduce the absorption or effect of vitamin A (retinol). Take them at least 2 hours apart.

evidence_text: The Xenical datasheet (NZ Medsafe) reports that in a pharmacokinetic study, oral amiodarone given during orlistat treatment showed a 25-30% reduction in systemic exposure to amiodarone and desethylamiodarone. The 2012 US label checked does not mention amiodarone.
